Consult Summary:
- 48-year-old man with 3 days of acute watery diarrhea and preceding vomiting, now resolved; currently experiencing dehydration and weakness, likely due to gastroenteritis.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Acute onset diarrhea for 3 days.
- Timeline: Symptoms started 3 days ago with vomiting (occurred a couple of times), which has since resolved, followed by ongoing watery, loose stools (5–6 times daily).
- Progression: Vomiting resolved after initial onset; diarrhea persistent; no improvement reported.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Attempts to drink fluids but continues to feel dehydrated; limited oral intake due to poor appetite.
- Associated symptoms: Feeling very weak, reports dehydration. No abdominal pain, headache, or muscle aches. Felt a bit warm and possibly febrile at onset, but currently afebrile.
- Systems review: Negative for blood in stool, no recent sick contacts, and no suspicious food exposure reported.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma (uses inhaler—blue inhaler—dose/route/frequency not documented; uses only infrequently as needed).
- No drug allergies known.
- No other regular medications reported.

Social History:
- Lives alone.
- Works as a software engineer.
- Has been unable to work for last 3 days due to illness; normally employed.
- Non-smoker.
- Drinks alcohol infrequently, only socially.
- No substance use reported.

Family History:
- Father had hypertension and died of bowel cancer 10 years ago.
- Mother has type 2 diabetes.

Physical Examination:
- No physical examination or vital signs documented.

Investigations:
- No investigations, imaging, or lab tests documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Gastroenteritis (suspected viral or infectious cause)
  - Advise oral rehydration with increased fluid intake.
  - Recommend over-the-counter oral rehydration salts (brand mentioned: Dioralyte).
  - Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented) advised for fever or weakness as needed.
  - Advise time off work for another 1–2 days; must be diarrhea-free for 24–48 hours before return to work.
  - Monitor symptoms; if diarrhea persists beyond one week or worsens, advised to reconsult for reevaluation.
- General advice: Monitor for ongoing dehydration, recurrent or bloody diarrhea, worsening symptoms, or inability to keep fluids down—seek medical attention if these occur.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note, or fill document_quality):

● Allergies not formally denied, but "not that I know of" documented.
● No temperature, blood pressure, heart rate, or physical examination findings recorded.
● No stool description except watery/loose—no malodor, undigested food, or mucus discussed.
● No stool testing or relevant investigations initiated or planned.
● Asthma control and details of inhaler use not fully characterized.
● No medication, dose, or frequency for paracetamol documented.
● Transcript quality clear, no internal conflicts noted; mild conversational hesitations but clinical content preserved.
